**Step 1 — Scene:** A mixed fruit plate with what appear to be roasted Brussels sprouts.

**Step 2 — Vessel:** A shallow, roughly square plate, approximately 24 cm across. Using an equivalent circular diameter of about 25 cm gives an area of **491 cm²**.

**Step 3 — Items:** Orange/mandarin segments, strawberries, blackberries, raspberries, and roasted Brussels sprouts. No distinct sauce or dressing is visible; a light coating of cooking oil on the sprouts is possible.

**Steps 4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy:** Heights represent the average thickness of each food’s outer envelope. Density is the only allowance for gaps.

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = volume | Density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Orange/mandarin segments | 22% | 108 cm² × 1.8 cm = 194 ml | 0.65 | 126 g | 47 | 59 kcal |
| Strawberries | 13% | 64 cm² × 1.7 cm = 109 ml | 0.60 | 65 g | 32 | 21 kcal |
| Blackberries | 7% | 34 cm² × 1.5 cm = 51 ml | 0.60 | 31 g | 43 | 13 kcal |
| Raspberries | 3% | 15 cm² × 1.5 cm = 23 ml | 0.55 | 13 g | 52 | 7 kcal |
| Roasted Brussels sprouts | 16% | 79 cm² × 2.2 cm = 174 ml | 0.65 | 113 g | 70 | 79 kcal |

The areas sum to **61% coverage**. The sprouts’ energy estimate includes a modest cooking-oil allowance, rather than adding an unobservable separate oil serving.

**Step 8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **348 g and 179 kcal** is plausible for this moderately covered plate of fruit and several small roasted sprouts. The main uncertainties are plate size and cooking oil.
